ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-05-15
Provider: Dr. Aisha Johnson, MD
Department: Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Ongoing concerns about his speech and language development, with difficulty following instructions and limited vocabulary.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He returns for ongoing evaluation following pediatric and otolaryngology assessments in January and March 2020 for speech and hearing concerns. His parents report that he speaks in two-word phrases, has difficulty following simple instructions, and often seems frustrated when trying to communicate. They also note that he frequently repeats the same phrases and has a limited vocabulary compared to his peers.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Language disorder (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Conductive hearing loss (diagnosed 2020-03-15)
- Chronic otitis media with effusion
- Bilateral conductive hearing loss
- Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder

His birth and developmental history are unremarkable, and he has achieved appropriate motor milestones for his age.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
The parents deny any family history of developmental disorders.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child is noted to have normal hearing and no abnormalities in oropharyngeal structure. His social interaction with the parents is appropriate, but he avoids eye contact with the examiner and has a limited response to verbal stimuli. His growth parameters are within normal limits.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory values:
- Complete blood count: within normal limits
- Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH): within normal limits
- Lead level: within normal limits

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-03-15
Provider: Dr. Michael Patel, MD
Department: Otolaryngology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Parental concerns about his speech and language development, specifically not responding when called from another room.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for otolaryngology evaluation of speech and language concerns initially identified at his three-year well-child visit two months ago. His parents report that he is not speaking as well as his older sibling did at the same age and seems to have difficulty following simple commands. They also note that he often does not respond when called from another room, although he does turn to look at them when they speak to him face-to-face.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Language disorder (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Chronic otitis media with effusion
- Bilateral conductive hearing loss
- Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder

His birth history is unremarkable, and he has met all other developmental milestones on time.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with history of recurrent otitis media requiring tympanostomy tubes during childhood
- Older sister with resolved articulation disorder treated with speech therapy
- Maternal cousin with developmental language delay

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Preschool student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the child does not respond to noises outside his field of vision. Otoscopic examination reveals dull tympanic membranes with limited mobility on pneumatic otoscopy. There is no evidence of acute infection or effusion. The rest of the physical examination is normal.

Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the pediatric clinic for a scheduled 3-year well-child visit.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His parents say he is very active and enjoys playing at the park and with his older sister. He can run, climb stairs with alternating feet, and jump in place. He stacks nine blocks and recently began scribbling with crayons. He responds to his name, follows simple commands, and gestures when he wants something. He says a few single words such as "ball," "juice," and "go," but does not yet combine words into phrases. He does not ask questions or label objects consistently.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Chronic otitis media with effusion
- Bilateral conductive hearing loss
- Mixed receptive-expressive language disorder

His hearing screen at age 2 was normal.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with history of recurrent otitis media requiring tympanostomy tubes during childhood
- Older sister with resolved articulation disorder treated with speech therapy
- Maternal cousin with developmental language delay

SOCIAL HISTORY:
